title: Mirabai Chanu Will Lead India's Weightlifting Charge at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games
excerpt: The Olympic silver medallist headlines a seven-strong squad for Glasgow 2026, with Birmingham medallists Bindyarani Devi and Harjinder Kaur also named. Four debutants join the team.
body:
Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu has been named to lead India's weightlifting contingent at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, scheduled for July 23 to August 2. The two-time Commonwealth Games gold medallist will compete in the women's 48kg category — a weight class in which she has long been among the world's best.

## A Career Built on Big Stages

Chanu's Commonwealth Games record speaks for itself: gold in Gold Coast 2018, gold in Birmingham 2022, and a silver way back in Glasgow 2014 — the very city she returns to this summer. Add to that a silver medal at the Tokyo Olympics, a world championship title, and three new national records set at the February 2026 nationals in Modinagar, and the 31-year-old from Manipur remains India's most decorated weightlifter.

She did miss the Asian Weightlifting Championships in May while recovering from a shoulder injury sustained earlier this year, but her national championship performance — where she lifted 89kg in the snatch and 116kg in the clean and jerk for a 205kg total in the 48kg class — was emphatic enough to silence any fitness questions.

## The Squad Behind the Star



> **""I will keep my weight within 48kg till the Commonwealth Games, but within two months of it, there are Asian Games, which is in 49kg, so I will have to switch back," Chanu said earlier this year."**


Chanu will be joined by fellow Birmingham 2022 silver medallists Bindyarani Devi (women's 58kg) and Harjinder Kaur (women's 69kg). In the men's division, Lovepreet Singh, a bronze medallist from the last edition, will compete in the +110kg category.

Three men make their Commonwealth Games debut: Rishikanta Singh (60kg), Ajaya Babu (79kg), and Dilbag Singh (94kg). Together, the seven lifters represent a squad that blends proven medal-winning experience with fresh talent.

## The Weight Category Juggle

The International Weightlifting Federation's revised weight categories have added a layer of complexity to Chanu's 2026 calendar. Her old 49kg category no longer exists, so she will compete at 48kg in Glasgow. But the Asian Games in Nagoya, scheduled just two months later in September, use the 49kg division.

"I will keep my weight within 48kg till the Commonwealth Games, but within two months of it, there are Asian Games, which is in 49kg, so I will have to switch back," Chanu said earlier this year. The transition demands meticulous planning around nutrition, training loads, and recovery — the kind of marginal optimisation that separates the world's best from the rest.

## India's Weightlifting Pedigree at the CWG

India has historically punched above its weight in weightlifting at the Commonwealth Games. In Birmingham 2022, the country won three golds, three silvers, and four bronze medals — ten medals in total from weightlifting alone, making it one of India's most reliable medal factories at the multi-sport event.

Glasgow 2026 will test whether that dominance can continue under a revamped weight category system and against an increasingly competitive field.

## Why NRIs Should Care

For the Indian diaspora in the UK — and particularly in Scotland — Glasgow 2026 is the closest a major multi-sport event gets to home. Chanu's return to the city where she won her first Commonwealth medal in 2014 adds a storybook quality to the campaign. With a sizeable Indian and South Asian community in Glasgow and across Scotland, the Commonwealth Games will be one of the summer's most accessible chances for NRIs in Britain to watch Indian athletes compete live.

*Sources: Olympics.com, ANI, India Sports Hub, Indian Weightlifting Federation*
